summary: A request from the University of Utah for comments on making its Univac 1108 computer, running EXEC 8, available to the ARPANET. Interest had been shown at the ICCC conference, and since the 1108 already talked to the Utah PDP-10, little programming effort would be needed.

plainLanguage.summary: The University of Utah asked whether network users wanted access to its Univac 1108 computer. The RFC describes available equipment, software, rates and priorities to help readers assess the proposal.

questions: what computing resources did utah offer on the network
what priority system did utah propose for computer access
what was the proposed utah 1108 service
subtitle: A request for feedback on a possible Utah Univac 1108 service

tldr.problem: The University of Utah was considering making its Univac 1108 available to network users and asked whether the service would be useful.
tldr.mechanism: The notice describes the computer, its software and peripherals, along with proposed priorities, rates and operating times.
tldr.outcome: The RFC seeks comments; it does not announce that the 1108 was already available through the network.

today: RFC 403 is a request for comments on a possible Univac 1108 network service. The text describes the facilities and schedules but does not confirm that network access began.

sections.title: Considering a Network 1108 Service
sections.content:
The University of Utah had a Univac 1108 running EXEC 8. Some interest in making it available to ARPANET users had been expressed at the recent ICCC conference, but the computer was not then available on the network. Because it already communicated with Utah's PDP-10, the author says adding network use would require little programming effort.

The notice asks readers whether such a service would be desirable.
sections.plainLanguage: Utah was considering offering its Univac 1108 to network users. The author asks whether people would use it.

sections.title: Computer and Software Resources
sections.content: The Computer Center describes the 1108's storage, tape drives and high-speed drums, plus equipment for time-sharing and remote batch work. It also lists a large plotter, an optical scanner and a digitizer. The software list includes programming languages, an editor, an assembler, scientific and statistical routines, simulation packages and a linear programming program.
sections.plainLanguage: The notice lists the computer's storage, input and output equipment, and software. These details show what kinds of work the proposed service could support.

sections.title: Rates, Priorities and Availability
sections.content: The RFC includes schedules for job priorities, computing charges and other services. It says priorities apply to batch and remote batch work, while teletype or interactive service receives a priority rate based on the lowest priority then being accepted. It also gives a weekly schedule and advises readers to call the Computer Center to confirm operating status before on-site work.
sections.plainLanguage: Users could compare the listed rates and time periods before choosing how to run a job. The center advised checking its current status before travelling to use it.
